points.point: The AI data center technology change documented in the Vault is the move from the 48 V ecosystem to 800 V / ±400 Vdc HVDC as rack power reaches MW class
points.label: missing
points.why: does not mention 48 V to 800 V / ±400 Vdc HVDC or MW-class racks

points.point: The Vault's AI server ecosystem → R&S solution mapping assigns VNA, oscilloscope and phase-noise instruments (ZNL/MXO/FSWP/ZNA/ZNB) to these needs, not signaling or non-signaling radio communication testers
points.label: partial
points.why: mentions PCB/SI/material measurements, but not the VNA/MXO/FSWP/ZNA/ZNB mapping or exclusion of radio testers

points.point: Even data center power-electronics topics (800V HVDC) are mapped in the Vault to MXO / FSWP / ZISO / BMS test, with no signaling tester involvement
points.label: missing
points.why: does not cover 800V HVDC mapping to MXO/FSWP/ZISO/BMS with no signaling tester

points.point: That mapping page is only a sales/test clue from an Excel conversion and is not a formal configuration or validated requirement
points.label: missing
points.why: does not state mapping is only an Excel sales clue, not a validated configuration

points.point: In the Vault, signaling vs non-signaling tester roles are defined for wireless device testing: CMX500 for R&D signaling, CMP180 for production non-signaling RF
points.label: covered
points.why: states CMX500 for signaling/R&D-type testing and CMP180 for production non-signaling RF

points.point: Non-signaling mode is tied to WLAN/cellular device production RF measurement speed, i.e. a device-test driver rather than a data center driver
points.label: covered
points.why: states WLAN production RF measurements use non-signaling mode to save time

points.point: The documented driver of new signaling-tester measurement capability is new wireless standards such as Wi-Fi 8 / IEEE 802.11bn
points.label: covered
points.why: ties signaling capability to Wi-Fi 8 / IEEE 802.11bn and other wireless standards

points.point: Signaling test content in the Vault is scoped to LTE / 5G / Wi-Fi UE RF, application-layer and protocol measurements within 400 MHz–8 GHz, with no data center scope
points.label: partial
points.why: lists LTE/NR/WLAN signaling scope, but lacks full 400 MHz–8 GHz/application/protocol framing and no data center scope

invented: AI data center changes increase requirements for MIMO, bandwidth and multi-port RF testing capability
